2. Aggregate pits and asphaltic or Portland Cement plants supplying the construction project are controlled by Federal, State and local air quality standards for atmospheric emissions.
3. Adequate control of emissions from on-site asphaltic or concrete batching equipment will be employed.
4. Aggregate materials used on the construction project must comply with the "Standard Specifications" regarding the P-200 sieve test. This test minimizes the amount of fines (or dust) associated with the aggregate allowed on the project.
5. Because this proposed highway project lies within the Southeastern Wisconsin Air Ouality Pegion, there will be no open burning of material removed from the right of way. This material will be hauled to a suitable sanitary landfill site or buried within the project limits in designated areas.
Freeway construction will cause many temporary changes in local travel patterns, traffic movements, and everyday activities. To minimize this disruption provisions will be made in the contracts for maintaining safe access and through service as designated by the State, County, and Municipal governments. All construction activities which conflict with highway traffic will be controlled through signing, signals, and flagmen, meeting the acceptable practices set forth in the construction contract. All construction activities will be closely supervised to be in conformance with OSHA (Occupational Safety and Health Act) which became effective in 1972. This law was passed to insure the safety of construction workers, inspectors, visitors to construction sites, as well as the general public.
